identity.real_world_identity_notes: First product of the revived Puma marque after Puma production ended in 1999: a mid-engined rear-wheel-drive sports car on a steel tubular chassis with a fibreglass body, a transverse rear 1,598 cc 16-valve four of 120 CV and a five-speed manual. AMS2 classes it under GT5 alongside the Ginetta G40.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. No automatic cut or blip was present, so the driver supplies the upshift lift.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.
Confidence is medium because the single reviewed source is a specification listing rather than a manufacturer or technical publication.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.puma-p052.20260814t045702852z-3d28884b by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the revived P052 and its five-speed manual, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The source states a 5-speed manual, rear-wheel drive with a 1,598 cc 16-valve four, and the live drive selected five H-pattern gears. Construction is inferred from an ordinary road-derived manual; no reviewed source states it.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Probably a synchronised gearbox, so the blip eases the synchros but should not be needed to engage the gear. Construction is inferred from a road-derived manual rather than stated by a reviewed source.
